# Development Release

This page is for contributors.
It tells how the types work, which workflows run in CI, how to make a release, and how to publish the wiki.
Read [Development](Development) first.

## Types

- The root `tsconfig.json` gives an editor the types of the Claude Code hooks module.
  It extends `plugins/claudetto/tsconfig.json`.
- Claude Code writes the `.claude-plugin/types/` folders and a `tsconfig.json` when an interactive session loads a plugin from your checkout, such as in `just sandbox`.
  Git ignores these files.
  `just check` needs them, and CI does not.
- A session with `-p` loads the plugins but does not write the types.
  So a new clone gets them only from an interactive session.
- A linked worktree has no types.
  `just typecheck` runs `tools/types.ts` first, which copies each missing `.claude-plugin/types/` folder and plugin `tsconfig.json` from the main worktree.
  When the file `plugins/claudetto/.claude-plugin/types/tsconfig.json` is still missing, the script stops and tells you to start an interactive session.
- Claude Code writes the types again at each load, from the tools of that session.
  The tools can differ between sessions, so a test gives no field that only some sessions have.

## Continuous Integration

The workflows are in `.github/workflows/`.

- `ci.yml` runs on each push and each pull request.
  Its `check` job runs `just ci` on Ubuntu and macOS.
  It installs `Bun` from `package.json`, `just` 1.58.0, and Claude Code 2.1.303.
  Its `all-green` job is the one to require in branch protection.
- `claude.yml` answers an `@claude` mention in an issue, a review comment, or a review, with `anthropics/claude-code-action`.
  It answers only users with write access.
  It needs the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` secret and the Claude GitHub App.
  Its steps skip when the secret is empty, so a fork has no failed run.
- `eval-new-claude-code.yml` runs `just eval` each day at 06:00 UTC, and from `workflow_dispatch`.
  It never runs on a pull request.
  It runs the evals for a release tag of `anthropics/claude-code` that is higher than the version in `ci.yml`.
  A cache entry marks each tag after the run, so each tag runs one time.
  Set the input `force` to run a marked tag again.
  A failed eval fails the run.
  Then fix the plugin, and set the version in `ci.yml` to the new release.

## Evals

`just eval --model M` runs `claude plugin eval` on the suite in `plugins/claudetto/evals/`.
It tests the checkout, and not the installed copy.
`--max-cost-usd 5` (`EVAL_MAX_COST_USD`) bounds its cost.
The recipe needs `--model`, such as `--model haiku`, because without it the eval uses the model of the session.
A lock stops a second run while one is in progress.
The suite format and the results are on [Evals](Evals).
Ask the owner of the repository before each new paid run.

## Releases

1. Add each change to `CHANGELOG.md`.
   When the version in `package.json` has no tag yet, it is the release in progress, so add the change under the heading of that version.
   Otherwise, add the change under the `## [Unreleased]` heading.
   `just bump` fails when that heading is missing.
2. Preview the bump, then bump the version.
   The level is `major`, `minor`, `patch`, or `X.Y.Z`.

   ```bash
   just bump minor --dry-run
   just bump minor
   ```

   `just bump` changes the `version` line of `package.json` and two lines of `CHANGELOG.md`.
   It moves the `[Unreleased]` entries under a dated heading.
3. Copy the version to each `plugin.json`, then commit the result.

   ```bash
   just generate
   ```

   Commit before you tag.
   `claude plugin tag` checks that each `plugin.json` agrees with its marketplace entry, and it stops on a dirty working tree.
4. Run `just release-check`.
   It fails while a row of `findings.md` of the change has a `Task` that is not `none`, `done`, or `(checked)`.
5. Preview the tags, then tag and push.

   ```bash
   just release --dry-run
   just release
   ```

`just release` checks the tree, the generated files, and the tag names of all plugins before it makes a tag.
So a bad manifest stops the release with no tag made.
It then pushes all tags to `origin` in one atomic push.
When a tag step or the push fails, it deletes the tags that it made.
The notes of each release are in [Release History](Release-History).

## Wiki

1. Edit a page in `src/wiki/`.
   `just generate` writes `wiki/` from it.
   Do not edit `wiki/` by hand.
   The test `tests/support/wiki-links.test.ts` checks that each link resolves and that each page name is unique.
2. Run `just wiki` to publish `wiki/` to the GitHub wiki.

> **Note:** The wiki repository exists only after the first page is made in the GitHub web UI.
